finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. require_admin calls abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The `except Exception` block catches it and only logs a warning, so execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users. The unban endpoint does not have this flaw.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST; uid is attacker-controlled
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block
abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException for non-admins
except Exception catches the HTTPException, which subclasses Exception
Only logs a warning; there is no return or re-raise
do_ban(uid) executes regardless of the admin check result

finding.guards_checked: require_admin checks is_admin, but its denial is swallowed by the broad except. There is no other decorator, before_request hook, or check in the file. The unban route at line 26 calls require_admin without try/except, so it is correctly guarded. Authentication of g.user is not defined in this file; the attack assumes any logged-in user. The log line also writes the user name, which is minor.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 on non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in try/except Exception (16-19), which swallows the HTTPException. No before_request hook or decorator exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20 the 403 HTTPException raised by abort() in require_admin (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` at line 18 and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any authenticated non-admin; the unban route (line 26) calls require_admin without try/except.
